title: Granny Stripe Shawl
subtitle: DK weight rectangle in granny stripe rows using three colours on a 4mm hook
excerpt: A rectangle shawl worked in the granny stripe: rows of 3-treble clusters with chain-1 gaps, worked in three repeating colours. DK weight on a 4mm hook produces a fabric with the character of a granny square but in a simple rectangular layout.

glossaryTerms.definition: A row-by-row construction using groups of 3 treble crochets separated by chain-1 spaces, worked into the chain spaces of the previous row rather than into stitch tops. Produces the same texture as a granny square but in a flat rectangular format.

To change yarn colour at the end of a row: work the final stitch of the last cluster up to the last yarn-over, then draw the new colour through the final loops to complete the stitch. Cut the old colour and continue with the new.

content.text: This shawl is a rectangle measuring approximately 180cm wide by 55cm deep, worked in the granny stripe stitch using three colours. The granny stripe is a row-by-row version of the granny square: instead of rounds, you work rows of 3-treble clusters with chain-1 spaces between them, and each new row's clusters sit over the chain-1 spaces of the row below. Colour changes happen at the end of every row, cycling through the three colours in order. DK weight on a 4mm hook produces a fabric with firm structure and clear colour stripes. The stitch repeat is consistent throughout: once you have worked the first two rows, the rest of the shawl follows the same sequence.

Yarn: approximately 200g each of three DK weight colours (approximately 600g total). Label these Colour A, Colour B, and Colour C. Hook: 4mm. You will also need a tapestry needle, scissors, and a tape measure. Stitch markers are helpful for checking the repeat at the start.
Gauge

One granny stripe repeat (3 tr cluster plus ch-1 sp) measures approximately 2.5cm wide on a 4mm hook over granny stripe pattern. 180cm width requires approximately 72 repeats. Work a swatch of at least 20 repeats to check your tension before casting on for the full width.
Stitches used
ch: chain
sl st: slip stitch
tr: treble crochet (UK)
Granny stripe: 3 tr in ch-1 sp, ch 1, repeat
Colour change at end of row
Pattern

The foundation chain sets the width of the shawl. The granny stripe repeat is 4 chains (3 tr + 1 ch gap), plus 3 chains for the turning chain at the start of Row 1. For 72 repeats the foundation chain is: 72 x 4 = 288, plus 3 = 291 chains total.
Foundation chain (Colour A)
Using Colour A, ch 291. Lay flat and measure: should reach approximately 180cm.
Row 1 (Colour A)

Ch 3 (counts as first tr), 2 tr in 4th ch from hook, [ch 1, skip 3 ch, 3 tr in next ch] across to last 4 ch, ch 1, skip 3 ch, 3 tr in last ch. Change to Colour B on final yarn-over of last cluster, turn. (72 clusters, 71 ch-1 sps)
Row 2 (Colour B)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr), 2 tr in first ch-1 sp, [ch 1, 3 tr in next ch-1 sp] across. Change to Colour C on final yarn-over, turn. (72 clusters, 71 ch-1 sps)
Row 3 (Colour C)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr), 2 tr in first ch-1 sp, [ch 1, 3 tr in next ch-1 sp] across. Change to Colour A on final yarn-over, turn. (72 clusters, 71 ch-1 sps)
Following rows

Repeat Rows 2 and 3, cycling A, B, C in order. Each row is identical in structure: ch 3, 2 tr in first ch-1 sp, [ch 1, 3 tr in next ch-1 sp] across, change colour on final yarn-over. Continue until the work measures approximately 55cm from the foundation chain edge. At the stated gauge this is approximately 22 rows. End with a complete set of all three colours if possible, finishing after a Row C. Fasten off.
Edging (optional)

Join Colour A at any corner. Work one round of dc evenly around all four sides, placing 3 dc in each corner. Sl st to join, fasten off. This stabilises the edges and tidies the colour-change selvedge.
Finishing

Weave in all colour-change tails on the wrong side. There will be two tails per row end (one from the finished colour and one from the new colour). Weave each tail along a row of stitches in a matching colour direction so it does not show from the front. Block by soaking briefly in cool water, pressing out moisture in a towel, and pinning to the stated dimensions on a foam mat.
Care
Hand wash or machine wash on a gentle cool cycle depending on the yarn fibre. Check the label. Reshape and dry flat. Do not tumble dry at high heat.
What to try next

The granny stripe translates directly into a blanket: use a longer foundation chain and the same three-colour rotation. For a shaped version using the same stitch, a granny stripe triangle shawl adds increases at the edges in the same way the V-stitch triangle shawl does. If you want to use the granny stripe structure in the round rather than in rows, a granny square sampler blanket is the natural progression.
